evidence: services/.../browser/UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no args, but the only definition is UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (grep finds no zero-arg overload). This is a compile error. Passing context.getUser() fixes it. Inside the `context.getUser() != null` branch the call then reduces to webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled(), which matches the intended behavior: don't skip the form on re-auth when passkeys are enabled.

PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:291-296 wraps driver.findElement(...) in assertThat(..., nullValue()). Selenium's findElement throws NoSuchElementException and never returns null, so the nullValue() matcher is dead code. catch(Exception) is broad: it would also swallow unrelated WebDriver failures such as StaleElementReference or a lost session. It does NOT swallow fail(), because AssertionError is an Error, so the test still catches a button that is present. The sibling test PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202 already uses Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...), so the suggestion matches existing convention. The same pattern appears in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest (diff hunk).

PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:312-317 is the same try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception) pattern as issue 1. It works, since fail() throws AssertionError, which escapes catch(Exception), but it is misleading and too broad. Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as used in PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202 is cleaner.
PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:413 comment reads '// Succesful event - password login'. This is a typo for 'Successful', in a comment only, so it has no functional impact.
